questions.prompt: Reflection angles are measured from the…
questions.explanation: The normal is perpendicular to the surface at incidence.

questions.prompt: A plane mirror image is…
options: Formed on the mirror surface itself
questions.explanation: Reflected rays appear to come from behind the mirror.

questions.prompt: The angle of reflection equals the angle of…
options: Any angle chosen by the observer
questions.explanation: The law of reflection is i = r.

questions.prompt: An object is partly hidden by a card near a mirror. It can remain visible when…
options: The card creates its own image source
An object–mirror–eye path passes around the card
questions.explanation: Trace the full path; a card blocks only the rays it intersects.

questions.prompt: A plane mirror is often said to reverse left and right. A more precise description is…
options: It reverses the direction perpendicular to its surface
It rotates every object through 180° vertically
It swaps up and down in all cases
It changes the object’s actual handedness physically
questions.explanation: Reflection reverses the front–back coordinate; apparent left–right swapping depends on how we compare views.

questions.prompt: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 15° to the normal. What is its reflection angle to the normal? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Use i = r; both angles are measured from the normal. Result: 15 °.

questions.prompt: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 25° to the normal. What is its reflection angle to the normal? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Use i = r; both angles are measured from the normal. Result: 25 °.

questions.prompt: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 35° to the normal. What is its reflection angle to the normal? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Use i = r; both angles are measured from the normal. Result: 35 °.

questions.prompt: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 50° to the normal. What is its reflection angle to the normal? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Use i = r; both angles are measured from the normal. Result: 50 °.

questions.prompt: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 70° to the normal. What is its reflection angle to the normal? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Use i = r; both angles are measured from the normal. Result: 70 °.

questions.prompt: A ray entering a higher refractive index at an oblique angle usually bends…
options: Along the surface in every case
questions.explanation: Its speed decreases and the ray bends towards the normal.

questions.prompt: During refraction at a stationary boundary, which remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: The source determines frequency; speed and wavelength change together.

questions.prompt: Which equation is Snell’s law?
options: n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r
n₁ cos i = n₂ sin r in all cases
n₁i = n₂r exactly for all angles
questions.explanation: Snell’s law relates sines of angles measured from the normal.

questions.prompt: At normal incidence into glass, a light ray…
questions.explanation: Incidence zero gives refraction zero, but the speed changes.

questions.prompt: A ray moves from glass into air below the critical angle. Its transmitted wavelength…
questions.explanation: Speed increases while frequency stays constant, so λ increases.

questions.prompt: Light enters glass of index 1.50 from air of index 1.00 at 10° to the normal. Find the refracted angle. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: r = asin(n₁ sin i/n₂). Use degree mode. Result: 6.65 °.

questions.prompt: Light enters glass of index 1.50 from air of index 1.00 at 20° to the normal. Find the refracted angle. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: r = asin(n₁ sin i/n₂). Use degree mode. Result: 13.2 °.

questions.prompt: Light enters glass of index 1.50 from air of index 1.00 at 30° to the normal. Find the refracted angle. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: r = asin(n₁ sin i/n₂). Use degree mode. Result: 19.5 °.

questions.prompt: Light enters glass of index 1.50 from air of index 1.00 at 45° to the normal. Find the refracted angle. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: r = asin(n₁ sin i/n₂). Use degree mode. Result: 28.1 °.

questions.prompt: Light enters glass of index 1.50 from air of index 1.00 at 60° to the normal. Find the refracted angle. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: r = asin(n₁ sin i/n₂). Use degree mode. Result: 35.3 °.

questions.prompt: TIR requires light to go from…
options: Any medium into any other at 0°
questions.explanation: The refracted angle can reach 90° only for the higher-to-lower direction.

questions.prompt: Above the critical angle in an ideal TIR case, there is…
options: A transmitted ray at every angle
questions.explanation: The ideal geometric-optics model gives total reflection.

questions.prompt: At the critical angle the transmitted ray is…
questions.explanation: Refraction angle r = 90° at the critical angle.

questions.prompt: Which is an application of TIR?
options: Guiding light in an optical fibre
questions.explanation: A suitable higher-index core and lower-index surroundings can guide light.

questions.prompt: Why cannot light entering glass from air undergo TIR at that first boundary?
options: It is travelling from lower to higher index
questions.explanation: TIR requires the opposite index direction as well as sufficiently large incidence.

questions.prompt: A material of refractive index 1.3 meets air of index 1.00. Find the critical angle for light inside the material. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: sin c = n₂/n₁ = 1/n; c = asin(1/n). Result: 50.3 °.

questions.prompt: A material of refractive index 1.4 meets air of index 1.00. Find the critical angle for light inside the material. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: sin c = n₂/n₁ = 1/n; c = asin(1/n). Result: 45.6 °.

questions.prompt: A material of refractive index 1.5 meets air of index 1.00. Find the critical angle for light inside the material. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: sin c = n₂/n₁ = 1/n; c = asin(1/n). Result: 41.8 °.

questions.prompt: A material of refractive index 1.6 meets air of index 1.00. Find the critical angle for light inside the material. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: sin c = n₂/n₁ = 1/n; c = asin(1/n). Result: 38.7 °.

questions.prompt: A material of refractive index 1.8 meets air of index 1.00. Find the critical angle for light inside the material. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: sin c = n₂/n₁ = 1/n; c = asin(1/n). Result: 33.7 °.

questions.prompt: A converging thin lens has focal length that is…
options: Positive in the stated sign convention
Equal to object distance in every case
questions.explanation: Here real-object distance is positive and converging focal length is positive.

questions.prompt: A real image can be…
options: Located only by dashed back extensions
Formed by all diverging lenses with real objects
questions.explanation: Real rays converge at a real image, allowing a screen to intercept it.

questions.prompt: A real object inside a converging lens’s focal length forms a…
options: Real inverted image in every case
Real image at the focal plane
questions.explanation: Rays diverge after the lens; their backward extensions meet on the object side.

questions.prompt: A real object at twice the focal length of a converging thin lens forms an image…
options: At 2f, inverted and the same size
questions.explanation: The thin-lens equation gives v = 2f and m = −1.

questions.prompt: For an object exactly at the focal point of an ideal converging thin lens, emerging rays are…
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 0, so the image is at infinity in this ideal model.

questions.prompt: A converging thin lens has f = +10 cm and real-object distance u = 30 cm. Find v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Positive v means a real image. Result: 15 cm.

questions.prompt: A converging thin lens has f = +12 cm and real-object distance u = 36 cm. Find v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Positive v means a real image. Result: 18 cm.

questions.prompt: A converging thin lens has f = +8 cm and real-object distance u = 24 cm. Find v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Positive v means a real image. Result: 12 cm.

questions.prompt: A converging thin lens has f = +15 cm and real-object distance u = 45 cm. Find v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Positive v means a real image. Result: 22.5 cm.

questions.prompt: A converging thin lens has f = +5 cm and real-object distance u = 20 cm. Find v using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Positive v means a real image. Result: 6.67 cm.

questions.prompt: A diverging thin lens has focal length that is…
questions.explanation: A diverging focal point is virtual, giving f < 0 in this convention.

questions.prompt: With a real object, a diverging lens forms an image that is…
questions.explanation: For f < 0 and u > 0, v < 0 and 0 < magnification < 1.

questions.prompt: A negative image distance here means the image is…
questions.explanation: The sign indicates which side of the lens contains the image.

questions.prompt: Dashed extensions on a lens diagram represent…
options: A path through an opaque block
Backward extensions used to locate a virtual image
questions.explanation: Real light follows solid outgoing rays; the extensions show apparent origin.

questions.prompt: For a diverging lens with a real object, magnification m = −v/u is…
questions.explanation: Negative v and positive u give positive m, with a reduced upright image.

questions.prompt: A diverging thin lens has f = -10 cm and u = 30 cm. Find its signed image distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Keep f negative; negative v locates a virtual image. Result: -7.5 cm.

questions.prompt: A diverging thin lens has f = -12 cm and u = 24 cm. Find its signed image distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Keep f negative; negative v locates a virtual image. Result: -8 cm.

questions.prompt: A diverging thin lens has f = -8 cm and u = 16 cm. Find its signed image distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Keep f negative; negative v locates a virtual image. Result: -5.33 cm.

questions.prompt: A diverging thin lens has f = -15 cm and u = 45 cm. Find its signed image distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Keep f negative; negative v locates a virtual image. Result: -11.2 cm.

questions.prompt: A diverging thin lens has f = -5 cm and u = 20 cm. Find its signed image distance. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Keep f negative; negative v locates a virtual image. Result: -4 cm.

questions.prompt: A camera sensor normally receives an image that is…
options: Always the same size as the object
Formed behind a diverging lens alone
questions.explanation: A converging camera lens forms a real image on its sensor.

questions.prompt: Focusing a simple camera involves…
options: Changing the speed of light in vacuum
Matching sensor position to the image plane
questions.explanation: The sensor must intercept the converging rays at the required image distance.

questions.prompt: An object moves farther away from a converging camera lens. Required image distance approaches…
options: Minus the focal length for every photograph
questions.explanation: As 1/u approaches zero, v approaches f.

questions.prompt: Opening the aperture at fixed shutter time generally admits…
questions.explanation: A larger opening passes more of the available light; other photographic effects also matter.

questions.prompt: In the thin-lens camera model, changing aperture alone changes…
options: Focal length but not admitted light
The sign of all real-image distances
Admitted light, but not the focal length
questions.explanation: Aperture limits the ray bundle; the ideal lens focal length remains fixed.

questions.prompt: A camera lens has focal length 50 mm and object distance 1000 mm. Where should its sensor be, measured from the thin lens? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Use the same units for f, u and v, and solve 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Result: 52.6 mm.

questions.explanation: Use the same units for f, u and v, and solve 1/v = 1/f − 1/u. Result: 51.3 mm.
